title: ANTACONISM OF CHRONIC NICOTINE ADMINISTRATION ON SCHEDULE-CONTROLLED BEHAVIOR IN RATS
abstract: Twenty-four male rats were trained under a multiple schedule until responding was stable. The rats were anesthetized and an oseotic minipump filled with (-)-nicotine was inserted subcutaneously between the scapules. Nicotine was infused subcutaneously at 12 mg/kg and 16 mg/kg. After 240 hours of continuous nicotine infusion, the rats were challenged with the nicotinic-cholinergic antagonist mecaaylasine. Blood samples were collected from the dorsal digital vein in the hind paw under ether anesthesia the day before and the day after the mecaaylamice challenge. FI rates were significantly decreased on the first day and remained stable throughout the remainder of the nicotine phase. FR rates were also decreased on day 1 of nicotine exposure but this effect failed to achieve statistical significance. Beginning on day 3, FR rates were significantly elevated on 6 out of 10 sessions. The mecaaylasine challenge significantly decreased FR response rate, but this decrease was not significantly different from control values. FI performance was not altered during the mecaaylasine challenge. Multiple food detection analyses showed that nicotine levels were similar and that blood levels were 6.210.63 ng/ml.
